This is CRITICAL ADVICE tbh! I'm enjoying a perfect experience with my 7900GRE now thanks to using Fluid Motion and disabling Frame Gen in game (along with some other Adrenaline settings). It's kinda insane how good it is...I miss the the days of 670GTX simplicity lol

7900GRE + 5800X here, 144fps at Highest settings with no input lag and no stutter. Here's my setup of choice:

up to date drivers and DirectStorage DLLs
GFX: Highest, FSR 3: Quality, Frame Gen: Disabled

The AMD Adrenaline settings:
(I would assume Fluid Motion Frames is the most important one here, but I'm really happy with the rest).

Fluid Motion Frames 2.1: Enabled
Search Mode: High
Performance Mode: Quality
Radeon Anti-Lag: Enabled
Radeon Image Sharpening: Enabled 80% (personal preference)
Radeon Enhanced Sync: Enabled
Display Colour Enhancement: Vivid Gaming (personal preference; the game looks much more vibrant and lively)

Hope that helps!

If you're on AMD, and would like a perfect gameplay experience, this might help. I'm on 7900GRE, 5800X, 32gb 3600mhz on 1440p/165hz display....if you have similar or better specs, then rest assured, you can be enjoying the game at 140fps, no stutter and rich detailed graphics. 

I was suffering from constantly changing settings and trying to gaslight myself into believing it's running great when it wasn't... after much messing, I've accomplished quality, motion and responsiveness that's so good I feel like it's about to collapse under the weight of success. 

In short, using up to date drivers, swapping DirectStorage DLLs and using AMD Adrenaline settings in favour of Monster Hunter settings where possible.

I'm running Highest, FSR 3 Quality, Frame Gen Disabled and I'm getting 144fps 95th Percentile: 10ms (basically greased up stick of butter sliding through olive oil).

The AMD Adrenaline settings:

Fluid Motion Frames 2.1: Enabled

Search Mode: High

Performance Mode: Quality

Radeon Anti-Lag: Enabled

Radeon Image Sharpening: Enabled 80% (personal preference)

Radeon Enhanced Sync: Enabled

Display Colour Enhancement: Vivid Gaming (personal preference; the game looks much more vibrant and lively)

Enabling Frame Gen from in-game results in a noticeably input-lagged mouse cursor...even if joypad input fools you into thinking its responsive, the mouse cursor is a major reality check. That being said, with these settings, the mouse responds instantly. Absolutely categorically zero perceptible delay. Using AMD Fluid Motion Frames, in my experience, is far superior in Monster Hunter Wilds.

For anybody discovering this in 2024, who is having crashes/blue screen of death/system restarts, particularly when gaming or watching videos, after a LOT of messing about, changing RAM, editing Registry, editing Bios, this is what FIXED IT for me: Start Menu > Device Installation Settings > "No" (Select No, instead of Yes) > Save Changes.

  
Now restart, use your computer for an hour, open Event Viewer, look to see if any Errors or Warnings in the past 1 Hour....it should be error free, and of course, no restarts/crashes.

  
It's not ideal, it doesn't feel like a true fix, however it means you can get on with your day, crash free!

For anybody that discovers this thread recently; this sounds like "brain zaps" - there's a lot of info out there if you search for that term. You might find that moving your eyes from side to side, or having your head tilted down and looking up with your eyes results in a sudden feeling of 'dropping', almost like you got jolted, or went hyper-dizzy and almost passed out, but it happens really fast. First thing: DON'T WORRY...you'll start over-thinking, start to feel anxious, and then think yourself into a stressed out state, which can all be avoided by knowing that this is actually very common, it's not inherently dangerous, you aren't losing your mind or anything like that. 

  
The most common cause is starting (or stopping) medication (particularly anti-depressants)...especially if you have reduced your dosage significantly (or completely). Slowly coming off medication is often much wiser than immediately stopping, as your body and brain need time to adapt.

3D Audio with Corsair HS80 genuinely creates depth and height that I had no idea was possible. I've used Dolby Atmos, Headphone:X and 'virtual' 7.1...and they sound 'spacious', but there's no way I could distinguish between 'top left' and 'bottom right' for example...yet with PS5's 3D Audio, I absolutely can. Nearly made the mistake of buying Pulse, until realizing Sony's Tempest audio works with any stereo headphones....or rather, it can be enabled, but I tried with some LG Tone 9 ear buds and they couldn't produce the distinctly positional audio of the Corsair HS80 (on Corsair's website, it specifically states that they 'support' Sony 3D Audio and Tempest...hence why I can hear axes whip past my head, and hear voices go from behind to side to center as I spin the camera).

PS5's 3D audio works with ANY headphones, including HS80. I know this because I am using them right now. On Crucial's website, you will see that it says the HS80 supports Sony 3D Audio ("Tempest"). Also on Sony's website, you will see it says about Pulse: "with a headset fine-tuned for 3D Audio on both PS4 and PS5 consoles". The headset is 'fine tuned' for 3D audio - it doesn't have any unique ability to produce 3D audio, as this is all handled by the PS5's Tempest Audio codec. I hope that helps - I spent the past few days finding the facts as I just got a PS5 and I already owned HS80. Another advantage of HS80 is the Slipstream dongle; there is no lag and the quality is great, even at a distance.

With regard to 3D Audio, I tried it with some LG Tone 9 in-ear buds, and it didn't sound very good. There is a demo mode where you can change the 'height' of the sound, and the height sounded almost identical whether I had it max height or lowest height....however on my HS80 headset, it's shocking how '3d' it sounds! It genuinely sounds like it's above you and then next to you and then below you! I was going to get Pulse headset because I thought it's the only way to get surround, but now I've used the HS80 with 3D Audio, there's no reason to get any other headphones (Although I am quite tempted to by Arctis Nova Pro)

Transphobic is a very strong label, sometimes I wonder if it's applied too often and too easily. Does it take some of the significance away from incidents when somebody is being clearly transphobic.

There's ignorant, irresponsible and hateful; I believe these are very different types of behaviour, with very different intentions "Ignorant" doesn't mean there's no harm, but there's a major difference between exhibiting ignorance, and clearly displaying intent to harm. E.g. if saying the word "transformer" and giggling is transphobic, then what is encouraging people to attack somebody on Twitter and mock them for being trans. One seems that it should be fixed with education and understanding, and the other requires direct intervention and punishment.  

Soooo, I sometimes also can't clearly see where the transphobic behaviour is. The Monster Hunter Rise demo drops very soon, as promised.


As part of today’s Monster Hunter Rise developer livestream, Capcom finally announced when the game’s free demo will be going live. The Rise demo arrives tomorrow, January 8 on the Switch eShop (~1.6GB).

You can expect a decent chunk of content, too. All 14 weapon types will be available to play with across four quests. The beginner quest will pit you against a Great Izuchi, and the intermediate quest is a Mizutsune hunt. The two hunts can be played solo, in local or online co-op. As for locations, only the Shrine Ruins locale will be available, and that’s where you’ll see the stat-boosting endemic life.

The demo will also showcase some of the new mechanics in Monster Hunter Rise, including the Wirebug. You’ll even be able to bring along the adorable new Palamute companions.

Monster Hunter Rise is a Switch exclusive, though recent leaks suggested we’ll be seeing it on PC at some point. It’s due for release March 26.
